translationMethod: Source-compared translation; recitations retained in Arabic. Independent native/specialist sign-off is not claimed.

prayer-basics.howtopray1:
1. Intention
Intend in your heart to perform the required prayer for Allah while facing the qibla. Specify the prayer and whether its two, three or four rakahs are obligatory (fard), necessary (wajib) or sunna. For example: I intend the two obligatory rakahs of Fajr for Allah, facing the qibla. Spoken wording is an aid, not a replacement for the intention in the heart.

2. Opening takbir
prayer-basics.howtopray2:
After making the intention, raise the hands with the palms towards the qibla and say:
الله اكبر
In the traditional Hanafi description used in this guide, men raise their hands to the earlobes and women to the chest.

3. Standing and folding the hands
prayer-basics.howtopray3:
Place the right hand over the left. This traditional Hanafi guide describes men folding below the navel, with the right thumb and little finger around the left wrist and the other fingers resting on the left hand. It describes women keeping their fingers together and placing the right hand over the left at the chest.

4. Opening praise (thana)
سُبْحَانَكَ اللهُمَّ وَ بِحَمْدِكَ وَ تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَ تَعَالَي جَدُّكَ وَ لاَ اِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ

5. Al-Fatiha
Seek refuge in Allah, say the basmala, and recite Al-Fatiha:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْم، بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيْم، اَلْحَمْدُ للهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِيْنَ، الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيْمِ،
مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّيْنِ، اِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَ اِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِيْنُ، اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيْمَ، صِرَاطَ الَّذِيْنَ اَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ،
غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوْبِ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَ لاَ الضَّآلِّيْنَ، آمين

6. Further recitation
After Al-Fatiha recite another surah. Al-Ikhlas is an example:
قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ اَحَد، اَللهُ الصَّمَدُ، لَمْ يَلِدْ وَ لَمْ يُوْلَدْ، وَ لَمْ‌يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً اَحَد
Do not repeat the opening request for refuge before this additional surah.

7. Bowing (ruku)
prayer-basics.howtopray4:
Say the takbir and bow. In the traditional posture described here, a man keeps the head, neck and back level; the guide describes a more compact, less extended posture for women. Say slowly three times:
سُبْـحانَ رَبِّــيَ الْعَظِيْم.

8. Rising from bowing
Rise completely upright, saying:
سَمِعَ اللهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَه
Then say:
رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْد
When praying behind an imam, the follower says the latter response while the imam says the first phrase.

9. Prostration (sujud)
prayer-basics.howtopray5:
Say the takbir and lower yourself into prostration: knees, then hands, then nose and forehead. Keep the fingers together and place the face between the hands. This traditional guide describes men keeping their upper arms away from the sides and their abdomen away from the thighs, and women adopting a compact posture. Say slowly three times:
سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الاَعْلَي
Rise with the takbir, sit briefly, then make a second prostration and repeat the same remembrance three times.

10. Returning to standing
Rise with the takbir in the reverse order: lift the forehead and nose, then the hands and knees. This completes the first rakah.

11. Second rakah
Repeat the prayer sequence. Do not repeat the opening thana or request for refuge. Say the basmala, recite Al-Fatiha and another surah, then bow and prostrate as before.

12. Sitting for the testimony (tashahhud)
prayer-basics.howtopray6:
After the two prostrations of the second rakah, sit and recite:
اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ للهِ وَ الصّلَوَاتُ وَ الطَّيِّبَاتُ، اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ اَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَهُ اللهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ،
اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَي عِبَادِ اللهِ الصَّالِحِيْنَ، اَشْهَدُ اَنْ لاَّ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ الله وَ اَشْهَدُ اَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُوْلُهُ

13. Blessings on the Prophet
At the final sitting, recite:
اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَي مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَي اِبْرَاهِيْمَ وَ عَلَي آلِ اِبْرَاهِيْمَ اِنَّكَ حَمِيْدٌ مَّجِيْد.
اَللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَي مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِ مَحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَي اِبْراهِيْمَ وَ عَلَي آلِ اِبْراهِيْمَ اِنَّكَ حَمِيْدٌ مَّجِيْد.

14. Supplication
The original guide gives this supplication:
اَلَّلَهُمَّ اغْفِرْلِيْ وَ لِوَالِدَيَّ وَ لِاُسْتَاذِيْ وَ لِجَمِيْعِ الْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ وَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ وَ الْمُسْلِمَاتِ،
اَلاَحْيَآءِ مِنْهُمْ وَ الاَمْوَاتِ، رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَهً وَ فِي الآخِرَهِ حَسَنَهً وَ قِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ وَ احْشُرْنَا مَعَ الاَبْرَارِ بِرَحْمَتِكَ يَا اَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِيْنَ.

15. Closing salutations
Turn first to the right and then to the left, saying on each side:
السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَهُ اللهْ
This completes a two-rakah prayer.

16. A third rakah
For three-rakah Maghrib or Hanafi Witr, stand after the second-rakah tashahhud without reciting the final blessings yet. In obligatory Maghrib, recite the basmala and Al-Fatiha in the third rakah without an additional surah. Bow and prostrate, then sit for the tashahhud, blessings and supplication, and close with the two salutations.

In Hanafi Witr, recite Al-Fatiha and an additional surah in the third rakah. Before bowing, say the takbir, raise and refold the hands as described above, then recite the qunut:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اِنَّا نَسْتَعِيْنُكَ وَ نَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَ نُؤْمِنُ بِكَ وَ نَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْكَ وَ نُثْنِيْ عَلَيْكَ الْخَيْرَ، نَشْكُرُكَ وَ لاَ نَكْفُرُكَ، وَ نَخْلَعُ وَ نَتْرُكُ مَنْ يَّفْجُرُكَ.
اَلَّلهُمَّ اِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَ لَكَ نُصَلِّيْ وَنَسْجُدُ وَ اِلَيْكَ نَسْعَي وَ نَحْفِدُ، نَرْجُوْ رَحْمَتَكَ وَ نَخْشَي عَذَابَكَ اِنَّ عَذَابَكَ بِالْكُفَّارِ مُلْحِقْ.
Afterwards bow and prostrate, sit for the final recitations and close with the salutations. Witr is wajib in the Hanafi school.

17. A fourth rakah
In a four-rakah prayer, stand after the third rakah. Recite the basmala and Al-Fatiha. In sunna prayers add another surah; in the third and fourth rakahs of an obligatory prayer, the guide describes reciting Al-Fatiha alone. Complete the bowing and prostrations, sit for the final recitations and close with salutations to both sides.

wudu.vuzu_text1: Wudu is the ritual washing required before prayer when minor ritual impurity has occurred. It prepares the worshipper for prayer. The following steps describe the original Hanafi guide; the separate post-wudu remembrance has its own hadith reference.
wudu.vuzu1:
1. Seeking refuge and beginning in Allah’s name
Say quietly:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيْمِ
Meaning: I seek Allah’s protection from the rejected Satan and begin in the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
wudu.vuzu_text2:
2. Intention
Intend to perform wudu for Allah and to prepare for worship. The intention is in the heart.
wudu.vuzu2:
3. Washing the hands
Wash both hands up to the wrists three times, making sure water reaches between the fingers.
wudu.vuzu3:
4. Rinsing the mouth
Use the right hand to rinse the mouth three times. Clean the teeth with a miswak, toothbrush or fingers. When fasting, do not rinse so deeply that water may be swallowed. The original guide includes this supplication; its specific association with this step needs source review:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَعِنِّيْ عَلَي تِلاَوَهِ الْقُرْآنِ وَ عَلَي ذِكْرِكَ وَ شُكْرِكَ وَ حُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ.
wudu.vuzu4:
5. Rinsing the nose
Draw water gently into the nose with the right hand and clean it with the left, three times. The original guide includes this supplication:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَرِحْنِيْ رَائِحَهَ الْجَنَّه.
wudu.vuzu5:
6. Washing the face
Wash the whole face three times, from the usual hairline to below the chin and from ear to ear. Pass wet fingers through the beard as appropriate. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ بَيِّضْ وَجْهِيْ يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوْهٌ وَ تَسْوَدُّ وُجُوْهٌ.
wudu.vuzu6:
7. Washing the right arm
Wash from the fingertips to and including the elbow three times. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَعْطِنِيْ كِتَابِيْ بِيَمِيْنِيْ وَ حَاسِبْنِيْ حِسَاباً يِسِيْراً.
wudu.vuzu7:
8. Washing the left arm
Wash the left arm in the same way, including the elbow, three times. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ لاَ تُعْطِنِيْ كِتَابِيْ بِشِمَالِيْ وَ لاَ مِنْ وَرَاءِ ظَهْرِيْ وَ لاَتُحَاسِبْنِيْ حِسَاباً عَسِيْراً.
wudu.vuzu8:
9. Wiping the head and ears
Wet the hands and wipe the head. This guide describes wiping the whole head, then the inside of the ears with the index fingers and the backs of the ears with the thumbs. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِيْ مِنَ الَّذِيْنَ يَسْتَمِعُوْنَ الْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُوْنَ اَحْسَنَهُ.
wudu.vuzu9:
10. Neck wiping in the original guide
The older text describes wiping the two sides of the neck with the backs of the fingers and includes the following supplication. This is not an obligatory part of wudu; its recommendation and the specific supplication require scholarly source review:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَعْتِقْ رَقَبَتِيْ مِنَ النَّارِ.
wudu.vuzu10:
11. Washing the right foot
Wash the right foot up to and including the ankle three times, ensuring water reaches between the toes. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ ثَبِّتْ قَدَمِيْ عَلَي الصِّرَاطِ يَوْمَ‌ تَزِلُّ فِيْهِ الاَقْدَامُ.
wudu.vuzu11:
12. Washing the left foot
Wash the left foot in the same way, including the ankle, three times. The original guide includes:
اَلَّلهُمَّ اجْعَلْ سَعْيِيْ مَشْكُوْراً‌ وَ ذَنْبِيْ مَغْفُوْراً‌ وَ عَمَلِيْ مَقْبُوْلاً مَبْرُوْراً وَ تِجَارَهً لَنْ تَبُوُرَ بِفَضْلِكَ يَا عَزِيْزُ يَا غَفُوْرُ.
wudu.vuzu_text3:
Dressings and wounds
If water would harm an injured area, the original guide describes covering it with a clean dressing and wiping over the dressing while washing the unaffected parts. Ask a qualified scholar about the details of your condition.

Things that invalidate wudu in this Hanafi guide include using the toilet, passing wind, flowing blood or discharge, sleep that removes control, intoxication and loss of consciousness. Loud laughter during a prayer with bowing and prostration is also listed in Hanafi law. Not every form of sleep or every trace of blood has the same ruling; obtain guidance for doubtful cases.

ghusl.ghosl:
Ghusl: the full ritual bath
Ghusl removes major ritual impurity. In Hanafi law its obligatory elements are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole external body so that no required area remains dry.

A complete method
Make the intention, wash the hands, remove visible impurity and perform wudu. Wash the head and then the body thoroughly, including folds and areas beneath hair; beginning with the right side is recommended. If used water collects around the feet, wash them at the end. Immersion also requires water to reach the whole body and the mouth and nose to be rinsed; merely dipping into water does not replace these requirements.

When ghusl is required
Examples include ejaculation of semen with its relevant conditions, intercourse even without ejaculation, and the end of menstruation or postnatal bleeding. A wet dream requires ghusl when the relevant discharge is found. Pre-ejaculatory fluid (madhy) alone does not itself make ghusl obligatory; wash the affected area and perform wudu. Consult a qualified scholar if the nature of a discharge is uncertain.

This replaces ambiguous statements in the old guide; see the linked Hanafi sources.

tayammum.tayammom:
Tayammum: dry purification
The wudu and ghusl lessons explain purification with water. Tayammum can replace them when their legal conditions are met: water is unavailable after a reasonable search, the available water is needed to protect life, reaching it would be dangerous, or using it would cause a medically credible risk of harm. The old guide gives about two kilometres as an example of remoteness; precise legal conditions should be checked with a qualified Hanafi scholar. It is not simply a convenience when water can safely be used.
tayammum.tayammom1:
Method
Intend purification for an act requiring it, such as prayer. Touch a clean earth-based surface with both palms, shake off excess dust if needed, and wipe the whole face. Touch the surface a second time and wipe both arms, including the elbows: use the left hand for the right arm, then the right hand for the left. A third touch is not required for the second arm.

In the Hanafi description, appropriate clean earth-based surfaces include soil, stone, plaster, brick, marble and similar materials, whether or not loose dust is visible. Not every painted or coated surface qualifies automatically.

What ends tayammum?
Things that invalidate wudu also invalidate tayammum. When suitable water becomes safely available, its concession ends and the required washing must be performed. The scope of what an intention permits needs its legal conditions; ask a qualified scholar about an unclear case.

dhikr.tasbihat:
Remembrance after prayer
After the obligatory prayer and its associated sunna prayers, one may remember Allah. The following collection preserves the older guide’s recitations. Some particular counts are local devotional practices, not independently established here as a prescribed prophetic sequence. The remembrance itself and a claim about a particular fixed reward must be assessed separately.
dhikr.tasbihat1:
Recitation in the original collection — 33 repetitions
سُبْحَانَ اللَّه
dhikr.tasbihat2:
Recitation in the original collection — 33 repetitions
اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهْ
dhikr.tasbihat3:
Recitation in the original collection — 34 repetitions
اَللَّهُ اَكْبَرْ
dhikr.tasbihat4:
Recitation in the original collection — 1 repetition
لاَ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ اللهُ وَحدَهُ لَا شَرِیکَ لَه لَهُ المُلکُ وَ لَهُ الحَمدُ یَحیِی وَ یُمِیتُ وَ هُوَ حَیٌّ لَایَمُوتُ بِیَدِهِ الخَیر وَ هُوَ عَلَی کُلِّ شَیٍ قَدِیر
dhikr.tasbihat5:
Recitation in the original collection — 7 repetitions In the older guide this is listed after Fajr and Maghrib.
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَجِرنَا مِنَ النَّارِ
dhikr.tasbihat6:
Recitation in the original collection — 8 repetitions In the older guide this is listed after Fajr and Maghrib.
اَلَّلهُمَّ اَدخِلنَا الجَنَّةَ
dhikr.tasbihat7:
Recitation in the original collection — 10 repetitions
لاَ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ اللَّهْ
dhikr.tasbihat8:
Recitation in the original collection — 1 repetition
مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُوْلُ اللَّهْ
dhikr.tasbihat9:
Recitation in the original collection — 10 repetitions
اَلَّلهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَي سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَ سَلِّمْ
dhikr.tasbihat10:
Recitation in the original collection — 100 repetitions
اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهْ
dhikr.tasbihat11:
Recitation in the original collection — 20 repetitions
اَللهُمَّ يَا هَادِيْ
dhikr.tasbihat12:
Recitation in the original collection — 10 repetitions
اَلَّلهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَي سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَ سَلِّمْ
dhikr.tasbihat13:
Remembrance while bowing
سُبْـحانَ رَبِّــيَ الْعَظِيْم
dhikr.tasbihat14:
Remembrance in prostration
سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الاَعْلَي
dhikr.tasbihat15:
When rising from bowing
سَمِعَ اللهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَه
dhikr.tasbihat16:
Praise when standing after bowing
رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْد
dhikr.tasbihat17:
Opening praise
سُبْحَانَكَ اللهُمَّ وَ بِحَمْدِكَ وَ تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَ تَعَالَي جَدُّكَ وَ لاَ اِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ
dhikr.tasbihat18:
The testimony (tashahhud)
اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ للهِ وَ الصّلَوَاتُ وَ الطَّيِّبَاتُ، اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ اَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَهُ اللهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ،
اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَي عِبَادِ اللهِ الصَّالِحِيْنَ، اَشْهَدُ اَنْ لاَّ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ الله وَ اَشْهَدُ اَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُوْلُهُ
dhikr.tasbihat19:
Blessings on the Prophet
اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَي مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَي اِبْرَاهِيْمَ وَ عَلَي آلِ اِبْرَاهِيْمَ اِنَّكَ حَمِيْدٌ مَّجِيْد.
اَللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَي مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَي آلِ مَحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَي اِبْراهِيْمَ وَ عَلَي آلِ اِبْراهِيْمَ اِنَّكَ حَمِيْدٌ مَّجِيْد.
dhikr.tasbihat20:
Supplication in prayer
اَلَّلَهُمَّ اغْفِرْلِيْ وَ لِوَالِدَيَّ وَ لِاُسْتَاذِيْ وَ لِجَمِيْعِ الْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ وَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ وَ الْمُسْلِمَاتِ،
اَلاَحْيَآءِ مِنْهُمْ وَ الاَمْوَاتِ، رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَهً وَ فِي الآخِرَهِ حَسَنَهً وَ قِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ وَ احْشُرْنَا مَعَ الاَبْرَارِ بِرَحْمَتِكَ يَا اَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِيْنَ.
dhikr.tasbihat21:
Qunut in Hanafi Witr
اَلَّلهُمَّ اِنَّا نَسْتَعِيْنُكَ وَ نَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَ نُؤْمِنُ بِكَ وَ نَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْكَ وَ نُثْنِيْ عَلَيْكَ الْخَيْرَ،
نَشْكُرُكَ وَ لاَ نَكْفُرُكَ، وَ نَخْلَعُ وَ نَتْرُكُ مَنْ يَّفْجُرُكَ.
اَلَّلهُمَّ اِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَ لَكَ نُصَلِّيْ وَنَسْجُدُ وَ اِلَيْكَ نَسْعَي وَ نَحْفِدُ،
نَرْجُوْ رَحْمَتَكَ وَ نَخْشَي عَذَابَكَ اِنَّ عَذَابَكَ بِالْكُفَّارِ مُلْحِقْ.
dhikr.tasbihat22:
Supplication after prayer
The original guide places the following supplication after the obligatory prayers.
dhikr.tasbihat23:
The original collection’s supplication after prayer
اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهْ، اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهْ، اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيْمَ الَّذِيْ لاَ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّوْمُ‌ وَ اَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهِ.
اَلَّلهُمَّ‌ اَنْتَ‌ السَّلاَمُ وَ‌ مِنْكَ السَّلاَمُ، فَحَيِّنَا يَا رَبَّنَا بِالسَّلاَمِ، وَ اَدْخِلْنَا دَارَكَ دَارَ السَّلاَمِ،
تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَ تَعَالَيْتَ يَا ذَاالْجَلاَلِ وَ الاِكْرَامِ، لاَ اِلَهَ اِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيْكَ لَهُ،
لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَ لَهُ الْحَمْدُ يُحْيِيْ وَ يُمِيْتُ، وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لاَيَمُوْتُ، بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ، وَهُوَ عَلَي كُلِّ شَئٍ‌ قَدِيْرٌ

funeral.meyyet:
The funeral prayer (janazah)
This is a communal obligation: when a sufficient group performs it, the duty is discharged for the community; if nobody performs it, those responsible are accountable. The Hanafi method has four takbirs and standing, with no bowing or prostration. Its main recitations are praise of Allah, blessings on the Prophet and supplication for the deceased.

Be ritually pure, cover the required parts of the body, face the qibla and make the intention to pray for the deceased behind the imam. Say the opening takbir, fold the hands as in prayer and recite the opening praise quietly. The imam says the takbirs aloud; the followers recite quietly.
funeral.meyyet1:
Opening praise
سُبْحَانَکَ اَللَّهُمَّ وَ بِحَمْدِکَ وَ تَبَارَکَ اسْمُکَ وَ تَعَالَی جَدُّکَ وَ لاَ اِلَهَ غَیْرُکَ
funeral.meyyet2: After the opening praise, say the second takbir without raising or unfolding the hands again, according to the Hanafi method described here. Then recite blessings on the Prophet.
funeral.meyyet3:
Blessings on the Prophet
 اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، کَمَا صَلَّیْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَعَلى آلِ إِبْرَاهِیْمَ، إِنَّکَ حَمِیْدٌ مَجِیْدٌ،
اللَّهُمَّ بَارِکْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، کَمَا بَارَکْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِیْمَ، إِنَّکَ حَمِیْدٌ مَجِیْدٌ
funeral.meyyet4: After the blessings, say the third takbir without raising the hands. Make supplication for the deceased. For an adult man or woman the next supplication is given in the original guide.
funeral.meyyet5:
Supplication for an adult deceased person
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِحَیِّنَا وَمَیِّتِنَا، وَشَاهِدِنَا،
وَغَائِبِنَا وَصَغِیْرِنَا وَکَبِیْرِنَا، وَذَکَرِنَا وَأُنْثَانَا. اللَّهُمَّ مَنْ أَحْیَیْتَهُ مِنَّا فَأَحْیِهِ
عَلَى اْلإِسْلاَمِ، وَمَنْ تَوَفَّیْتَهُ مِنَّا فَتَوَفَّهُ عَلَى اْلإِیْمَانِ
funeral.meyyet6:
Meaning: O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, those present and absent, young and old, male and female. Keep those whom You give life upon Islam, and let those whom You take in death die upon faith.

For a boy who has not reached puberty, the original guide gives the following supplication.
funeral.meyyet7:
Supplication for a deceased boy
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ لَنَا فَرَطاً، وَاجعَلهُ لَنا َأَجْراً وذُخراً وَاجعَلهُ لناشافِعاً ومُشَفَّعاًً
funeral.meyyet8:
Meaning: O Allah, make him a forerunner, a reward and a treasure for us, and an intercessor whose intercession is accepted.

For a girl who has not reached puberty, the original guide gives the following wording.
funeral.meyyet9:
Supplication for a deceased girl
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْها لَنَا فَرَطاً، وَاجعَلها لَنا َأَجْراً وذُخراً وَاجعَلها لناشافِعاً ومُشَفَّعاً
funeral.meyyet10:
Meaning: O Allah, make her a forerunner, a reward and a treasure for us, and an intercessor whose intercession is accepted.

Say the fourth takbir without unfolding the hands, then finish with salutations to the right and left. No extra recitation is specified between this takbir and the salutations. Apart from the imam’s takbirs and salutations, the recitations are quiet. The old guide discourages adding a separate raised-hands supplication immediately after this prayer; consult a qualified Hanafi scholar about local practice.

sajdah-sahw.sejdesahv:
Prostrations for forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw)
Missing an essential pillar is not repaired merely by sujud al-sahw. The original Hanafi outline lists the opening takbir, standing where required, recitation, bowing, prostration and final sitting among the essentials. The details of ending the prayer also have legal conditions.

Forgetfully omitting or delaying a wajib can require sujud al-sahw. Examples in this guide include an extra bowing or prostration, omitting the tashahhud, forgetting Witr’s qunut, omitting Al-Fatiha or the additional surah where required, delaying the first sitting by reciting blessings, or an imam using the wrong audible/quiet recitation. Deliberate omissions and uncertain cases need separate rulings.

Method
At the end, recite the tashahhud, give one salutation to the right, make two prostrations, then sit and recite the tashahhud, blessings and supplication before the closing salutations. A follower does not independently depart from the imam’s sequence. Consult the linked Hanafi teaching for the precise situation; the old text’s distinction between solitary and congregational salutations should not be treated as a universal rule.

daily-prayers.dailypray:
The daily prayers in this Hanafi outline
Fajr: 2 sunna, then 2 obligatory rakahs.
Dhuhr: 4 sunna, 4 obligatory, then 2 sunna.
Asr: 4 obligatory rakahs in this basic list.
Maghrib: 3 obligatory, then 2 sunna.
Isha: 4 obligatory, then 2 sunna.
Witr: 3 wajib rakahs after Isha; it is a separate prayer.

This basic schedule totals 32 rakahs: 17 obligatory, 12 sunna and 3 wajib. It is not a claim that no other voluntary prayers may be performed. Ordinarily the daily sunna prayers are offered individually and the obligatory prayers in congregation where its conditions apply. Special practices such as Ramadan’s Tarawih have their own guidance.

friday.jomee:
Friday prayer (Jumuah)
The obligatory Friday prayer is two rakahs in congregation after the sermon, at Dhuhr time. Do not confuse these two obligatory rakahs with a total that includes additional sunna or voluntary prayers.

The standard Hanafi teaching includes four sunna rakahs before Jumuah and four after it; another transmitted practice adds two after those. Greeting the mosque is a separate voluntary prayer when appropriate. The old guide counted 18 rakahs by also including a precautionary Dhuhr and other local practices. That total is not the obligatory Jumuah itself, and these additions must not be presented as universally required. Ask a qualified local Hanafi scholar about a precautionary Dhuhr.

Ghusl, cleaning the teeth and suitable fragrance are recommended preparations. The obligation has conditions: for example, it does not apply in the same way to women or a legally defined traveller. Pray the obligatory Jumuah behind the imam; surrounding sunna prayers are offered individually.

congregation.jamaat:
Joining the congregation
Stand in the row, facing the qibla, and intend the appropriate obligatory prayer behind the imam. For example, a resident’s Dhuhr has four obligatory rakahs, not two. Say the opening takbir after the imam, recite the opening praise quietly and then listen to the imam’s recitation according to the Hanafi method.

Follow the imam in each posture and do not move ahead of him. When the imam rises from bowing with:
سَمِعَ اللهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهْ
respond:
رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْد
Follow him into the prostrations, reciting their remembrance quietly. In the sitting, recite the testimony, blessings and supplication as appropriate, and close after the imam’s salutations.

Arriving late
Join the imam in the posture in which you find him, but make the opening takbir while standing if able. After his final salutations, stand to make up the rakahs you missed. A rakah is counted only under its legal conditions; merely joining the final sitting is not a completed rakah.

Two-rakah prayer: if one was missed, perform one more and sit for the final recitations. If both were missed and you joined only the final sitting, perform both after the imam finishes.

Four-rakah prayer: make up one or two missed rakahs as required. If three were missed, the original outline describes performing one and sitting for tashahhud, then standing for the remaining two. If all four were missed, perform the full prayer with its sitting after the second rakah.

Three-rakah prayer: make up one missed rakah after the imam. If two were missed, perform one, sit for tashahhud, then perform the remaining one and the final sitting. If all three were missed, perform the ordinary complete three-rakah prayer. The details of recitation and sittings for a latecomer require Hanafi guidance; ask the imam if uncertain.

missed-prayers.ghaza:
Making up missed prayers (qada)
An obligatory prayer missed through sleep, forgetfulness or another cause must be made up. The prayer’s basic method remains the same; the intention identifies the missed prayer. For example: I intend the two obligatory rakahs of a missed Fajr for Allah, facing the qibla. If the exact date is unknown, identify the earliest or latest such prayer owed, according to the guidance you follow.

The older guide describes calling the adhan and an iqamah, with a separate iqamah for each prayer when making up several. These calls must not be confused with a condition without which an individual’s qada is invalid.

In Hanafi law, avoid the prohibited periods of sunrise, the sun’s zenith and sunset. The whole interval after Fajr is not itself the same as the actual sunrise prohibition for making up an obligatory prayer. Obtain local guidance on the boundaries of these periods.

eid.eyd:
Eid prayer
In the Hanafi description, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha prayers have two rakahs in congregation with additional takbirs. Intend the Eid prayer behind the imam.

After the opening takbir and opening praise, follow the imam in three additional takbirs, raising the hands as instructed. The imam recites Al-Fatiha and a surah, then the congregation bows and makes the two prostrations.

In the second rakah, the imam recites first. Then follow three additional takbirs, raising the hands; with the next takbir go into bowing. Complete the prostrations, final sitting and salutations as in prayer. Other schools have different additional-takbir counts; follow the selected school and the imam, rather than mixing methods.

travel.mosafer:
Prayer while travelling
The Quran speaks of Allah’s wish for ease:
یُرِیدُ اللّهُ بِکُمُ الْیُسْرَ وَلاَ یُرِیدُ بِکُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُکْمِلُواْ الْعِدَّهَ وَلِتُکَبِّرُواْ اللّهَ عَلَی  ‏مَا هَدَاکُمْ وَلَعَلَّکُمْ تَشْکُرُونَ.
Its meaning here is that Allah intends ease, not hardship, and gratitude for His guidance. This verse is in the context of fasting; the detailed rules of shortened prayer have their own evidence.

Qasr in this Hanafi guide
When the legal conditions of travel are met, the four obligatory rakahs of Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are shortened to two. Fajr remains two and Maghrib remains three. The rule concerns obligatory rakahs, not converting every sunna prayer into two.

The older guide uses approximately 82 km as its travel-distance estimate. Different Hanafi authorities express the legal distance with slightly different modern estimates. It is the intended qualifying journey, leaving the settlement boundary, and the legal length of the stay that matter; comfort or the type of vehicle does not remove the rule. Car, aircraft, ship, train or travel on foot can all be qualifying travel.

The guide’s example is a journey of 90 km: shortening starts after leaving the town’s boundary and may continue on the return journey until re-entering the home settlement. A stay intended for 15 days or more has a different Hanafi residency ruling. Ask a qualified scholar about connecting journeys, boundaries or an uncertain length of stay.

signs.ayat:
Eclipse prayer in the Hanafi school
During a solar eclipse, the Hanafi eclipse prayer consists of two voluntary rakahs, each with one bowing and two prostrations, in the pattern of an ordinary two-rakah prayer. It is sunna, not a new obligatory daily prayer. No adhan or iqamah is called for it. It may be led in congregation for a solar eclipse; for a lunar eclipse the Hanafi guidance cited here describes praying individually.

Lengthen the recitation and pray and supplicate during the eclipse, continuing remembrance and supplication if the prayer finishes before it ends. The older page’s method of five bowings in each rakah is not the Hanafi method and is not used here. This correction does not declare an obligatory five-bowing prayer for earthquakes or other frightening events.

night-prayer.tahajod:
Tahajjud: voluntary night prayer
Night worship is encouraged as a means of drawing near to Allah, seeking forgiveness and avoiding sin. It is a voluntary prayer, not an additional daily obligation.

Pray after Isha and before true dawn; the latter part of the night is especially suitable. The older guide describes sets of two rakahs, from two up to twelve. This is a practical outline, not an assertion that every other valid number is forbidden. Make the intention for voluntary night prayer and perform it like other two-rakah prayers, with sincere supplication.

qadr.ghadr:
Worship on Laylat al-Qadr
Its exact date is not known with certainty. Seek it during Ramadan’s last ten nights, particularly their odd nights, through prayer, Quran recitation, remembrance and supplication. Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.

Voluntary prayer can be offered in sets of two rakahs after Isha and during the night. The older guide proposed reciting Surah Al-Qadr once and Al-Ikhlas seven times in each rakah, followed by seventy repetitions of the following remembrance:
اَستَغفِرُاَللّهَ وَ اَتوبُ اِلَیه
These particular counts and this named sequence are not established here as an authenticated prescribed Sunnah. They must not be made a condition for obtaining the virtue of the night. Ask a qualified scholar before treating a fixed ritual or promised reward as a prophetic teaching.

ishraq.eshragh:
Ishraq prayer
After Fajr, remain in remembrance and Quran recitation if possible. Wait until the sun has risen sufficiently and the prohibited sunrise period has ended, then offer voluntary prayer. Do not pray at the instant of sunrise.

A report associates remaining in remembrance after congregational Fajr and then praying two rakahs with a great reward like Hajj and Umrah. This is an encouragement to sincere worship; it does not replace the obligatory Hajj. Check the linked source and local guidance for the timing.

awwabin.awabin:
Awwabin prayer in the older Hanafi guide
This refers here to voluntary prayer after Maghrib’s obligatory and sunna prayers. The guide describes six to twenty rakahs, offered in the normal manner, with an intention for voluntary worship.

A narration about six rakahs and a reward of twelve years’ worship is quoted in the older material, but that report is weak; do not present that precise reward as certain. Avoid idle or improper talk and worship sincerely. The name Awwabin is also used in other narrations for Duha; do not confuse the different uses.

tasbih-prayer.tasabih:
Salat al-Tasbih
This is a four-rakah voluntary prayer described in reports about the Prophet teaching his uncle Abbas. Scholars differ over the strength of its reports and its recommendation; it is not obligatory and should not be presented as a guaranteed solution to every hardship.

The repeated remembrance is:
 سُبحانَ اَللّهِ وَالحَمدُ لِلّهِ وَلا اِلهَ اِلاَّاَللّهُ وَ اَللّهُ اَکبَر

The method described in this guide uses 75 repetitions in each rakah:
After opening praise, before Al-Fatiha: 15.
After Al-Fatiha and the additional surah: 10.
In bowing, after its normal remembrance: 10.
After rising fully from bowing: 10.
In the first prostration, after its normal remembrance: 10.
Between the two prostrations: 10.
In the second prostration: 10.

Repeat this in each of four rakahs, with the normal sittings and final salutations: 300 repetitions altogether. Do not add an extra ten in the final sitting on top of this count. Some teaching traditions use a different distribution; follow a single verified method and ask a qualified scholar if uncertain.

tarawih.taravih:
Tarawih in Ramadan
Tarawih is voluntary Ramadan night prayer and an emphasized sunna in the Hanafi school for men and women. The original guide cites the report:
مَنْ قَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِیمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ
Its meaning is that one who stands in Ramadan in faith and seeking Allah’s reward receives forgiveness for past sins (Sahih al-Bukhari 2009).

The traditional Hanafi arrangement is twenty rakahs, offered in sets of two. Intend the two-rakah sunna prayer and follow the imam when praying in congregation. Its basic postures and recitations follow the ordinary prayer method. Do not confuse this school’s arrangement with a claim that every other school uses the same count.

greeting-mosque.tahiyatmasjid:
Greeting the mosque (Tahiyyat al-Masjid)
On entering the mosque, offer two rakahs before sitting when the legal conditions allow it. They are offered in the ordinary two-rakah manner with the intention of greeting the mosque.

The original guide cites Abu Qatadah’s report:
إذَا دَخَلَ أحَدُکُمْ الْمَسْجِدَ، فَلا یَجلِسْ حَتَّى یُصَلِّیَ رَکْعَتَیْنِ
Meaning: when one of you enters the mosque, he should not sit until he has prayed two rakahs (Sahih al-Bukhari 444; Sahih Muslim 714).

An obligatory or regularly associated sunna prayer performed upon entering can fulfil this greeting as well; a separate extra prayer is not always required. Consider prohibited times and the rules of the Friday sermon, and ask a qualified scholar if uncertain.
